tldr: About a third of your live ads are wearing out because you're running the same wording word-for-word across many ads at once. Meta treats those as basically one ad, so most of them are quietly getting shown to almost no one.

benchmark.context: The typical brand your size posts a fresh ad about every three weeks. The best brands do it every two. You should be closer to every ten days because you run this much volume.

ads.headline: Spend $149+, Get a FREE Face Mist 🤍
ads.body: Limited Time: FREE Full Size Face Mist 🎁  ✨ Spend $149+ and receive a FREE Full Size Hydra Balance Face Mist (Worth $32). A lightweight daily mist that hydrates, refreshes and leaves skin feeling calm. While stocks last.
drivers: You have four Face Mist gift ads live at once with almost identical wording, so Meta treats them as one and shows most of them to nobody.
This one has been running a month straight with no changes, well past when your ads normally start losing steam.
The 'Limited Time' and 'While stocks last' framing has been live for 30 days, which quietly tells shoppers the deadline isn't real.

ads.headline: Spend $149+, Get a FREE Face Mist 🤍
ads.body: A Little Extra, On Us. 🤍 Spend $149+ and we'll include a FREE Full Size Hydra Balance Face Mist (Worth $32). The perfect everyday refresh for growing skin. Limited time only.
drivers: This is the second version of the Face Mist offer running side by side with the first, splitting attention between two nearly identical ads.
Same headline, same offer, same page it sends people to as three other live ads, so Meta picks one and hides the rest.
One month in with no image or wording change, which is roughly double how long these should run before shoppers tune them out.

ads.headline: Designed for Kids
ads.body: Growing skin doesn't need a complicated routine ✨ It simply needs gentle, age-appropriate care that children can use with confidence every day. A simple routine is easier to stick to, helping healthy habits become part of everyday life. Petite Skin Co. is specially formulated for growing skin, with gentle products made to support kids aged 7-14 as they learn to care for their skin 🤍
drivers: You have four live ads with the exact same 'Designed for Kids' headline and the exact same body paragraph, all pointing to the same page.
Meta sees these near-identical ads as basically one, so it shows one and stops running the others. You paid to make them.
Nothing in the wording tells a mum why to buy TODAY. No new product, no reason, no urgency.

Making four copies of one message means three of them are barely being seen, and the ad money you put behind them is largely wasted.
There's no proof, no review, no customer voice. Every sentence is the brand talking about itself.

The 'TikTok trends' opening line runs word-for-word in a second ad here too, so shoppers seeing both feel like the brand is on repeat.
A month into running with no refresh, which is past your normal window. Mums who scrolled past it three weeks ago are scrolling past it now.

hero_concept.hook: The bit of her routine we didn't plan for.
hero_concept.headline: Made for after netball.
hero_concept.primary_text:
Sports sweat, sunscreen, a hot cheek pressed against a car window on the way home. That's when her face actually needs help.

The Petite Skin Face Towel is soft enough for a 9-year-old, small enough for her school bag, and built to hold up after 100 washes. One quick wipe before the cleanser, and the routine takes 60 seconds instead of five minutes.

Add it to any kit and use code TOWEL10 for $10 off your first order.
hero_concept.visual_direction: One soft folded Face Towel resting on a light stone bathroom counter next to a small glass of water and a sprig of eucalyptus, morning window light, no faces.
hero_concept.fills_gap: Almost every live ad talks in general terms about 'growing skin' and 'gentle care', but none of them show a real moment in a mum's day. This ad picks one specific moment (after sport) and pairs it with a single product, so it feels new next to everything else you're running.
hero_concept.image_prompt: A photorealistic editorial product photograph featuring the product from the reference image, styled in a soft light-stone bathroom counter scene with a small clear glass of water and a single sprig of fresh eucalyptus arranged loosely to the side, with soft diffused morning window light casting gentle natural shadows. Calm, clean, premium Australian skincare aesthetic with warm neutrals and a fresh, unstyled feel. Square 1:1 composition with breathing room top and bottom for ad text overlay. CRITICAL - preserve the exact soft white/cream cotton terry face towel color and plush looped-terry texture exactly as shown in the reference - strictly NO grey, beige, pink, blue, patterned, or color-shifted fabric, NO smoothing the terry loops into flat weave, NO changing to microfiber or waffle weave. STRUCTURE - preserve the exact construction: single small square folded face towel with visible looped-terry pile on both sides, clean hemmed edges on all four sides, and any Petite Skin Co. printed label, tag, or embroidered branding shown on the towel preserved exactly as positioned in the reference. Do NOT add tassels, fringe, borders, embroidered patterns, or trim not present in the reference, do NOT change the towel to rectangular or oversized bath-towel proportions, do NOT unfold or restack the towel differently, do NOT remove or alter any brand label or tag shown on the product. Render the product's metal, color, finish, fabric, weave, stones, surface treatment, AND every visible construction detail (silhouette, closures, hardware count, pockets, sleeves, neckline, printed graphics) EXACTLY as they appear in the reference image. Do NOT change the metal type, do NOT shift the color temperature, do NOT introduce tones not present in the reference, do NOT add or remove buttons, snaps, zippers, pockets, straps, or any hardware, do NOT alter the silhouette, do NOT remove or modify printed graphics or text on the garment. IMPORTANT: the 'no text' and 'no logos' items in the NEGATIVE list below apply ONLY to text or logos added as overlay to the photograph itself - text, logos, graphics, prints, and brand labels that exist ON the product in the reference image are part of the product and must be preserved exactly. Premium commerce photography quality. NEGATIVE: no overlay text added to the photograph, no overlay logos added to the photograph, no watermarks, no UI elements, no Facebook interface, no clickable buttons, no faces, no models, no collage, no borders, no duplicate products, no color shift, no metal swap, no silver-to-gold or gold-to-silver conversion, no warm-tone bias on cool metals, no recoloring of fabric or stones, no pattern modifications, no removing or replacing the product's printed graphics, no extra hardware not present in reference, no added pockets or pleats, no silhouette alterations, no design modifications.
